reason: The text explicitly describes the congregation (כל־ הָעֵדָה - 'kol ha-edah', all the assembly) murmuring and complaining against the princes/leaders (הַנְּשִׂיאִים - 'ha-nesiim'): 'And all the congregation complained against the leaders.' This murmuring (יִלֹּנוּ - 'yillonu') represents antagonism directed at the leadership structure, including Joshua, regarding their decision to make a covenant with the deceptive Gibeonites. The people's complaint is documented and constitutes genuine opposition to a leadership decision, though expressed through murmuring rather than violent resistance.
